tasks.title: Condense task journals

tasks.title: Thin old transcripts
tasks.what: A loop's transcript (every model and agent turn: its prompt, reply and tool calls) keeps its last days whole; an older turn keeps only what usage counts -- when, who, tokens, cost, whether it failed and why. tasks.title: Prune old agent folders
tasks.what: A loop's working folders of passes started more than the days ago (each agent's prompt, drafts and scratch) go -- its newest folder always stays, and the journal, the transcript, the record and the workbench. Running loops too: an old pass's folder is not written to.

tasks.title: Prune stale records
tasks.what: Record rows measured under other inputs (D853): the loop no longer counts them. Reports them; deletes them when told to.

tasks.title: Prune empty starts
tasks.what: Starts that did nothing -- stopped before any search, design, check or measurement began (D987) -- go: their row, and for a loop's latest start its log and journal. Starts already checked are left.

tasks.title: Rerun baseline
tasks.what: The loop's next start measures pass 0 again, once (D1005): otherwise a baseline on record stands while the document's baseline: section is unchanged, whatever else changed.

tasks.title: Invalidate + re-evaluate all
tasks.what: After the checks or measurement scripts change (D988): one run checks and measures every design on record again; the earlier results stay as history, no longer counted. Started on one loop only.

tasks.title: Check database integrity

"""The stage of ada_tune: measure the setting, print `name=value`. Usage: bench.py <block> <order>"""

import os
import sys
import time

# one BLAS thread: a timing that depends on how many cores the library grabbed is not repeatable
for var in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ.setdefault(var, "1")

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402 -- after the thread settings

from workload import matmul  # noqa: E402

block, order = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
n = 512
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
a, b = rng.standard_normal((n, n)), rng.standard_normal((n, n))
best = float("inf")
for _ in range(3):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    matmul(a, b, block, order)
    best = min(best, time.perf_counter() - t0)
print(f"time_ms={best * 1000:.2f}")

/file?path=check.py.x:
"""The gate of ada_tune: is the setting still correct? Runs the workload small and compares it with
a reference; prints `N failing`. Usage: check.py <block> <order>"""

import sys

import numpy as np

from workload import matmul

block, order = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
failing = 0
for n in (1, 7, 64, 100):
    a, b = rng.standard_normal((n, n)), rng.standard_normal((n, n))
    if not np.allclose(matmul(a, b, block, order), a @ b):
        failing += 1
        print(f"FAIL n={n}")
print(f"{failing} failing")

# Tuning: every point of `space:` is a setting passed to the gate and the stage as `{knob}`.
#     flux task run ./ada_tune --passes 15      # a pass a point (D738)

statement: >-
  The fastest block size and loop order for the blocked matrix multiply in workload.py.
language: text

flow:
  orchestrate:
    policy: sweep  # or gradient, anneal, genetic, pareto
    space:
      block: [16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
      order: [ijk, ikj, jki]
  test:
    test: {run: "{python} {home}/check.py {block} {order}", timeout_s: 60}
  measure:
    bench:
      command: "{python} {home}/bench.py {block} {order}"
      metrics: [time_ms]

objectives:

budget: {steps: 1, workers: 1}  # one timing at a time
